chosen.premise: Machop is only 0.8 meters tall yet can hurl 100 adult humans.
chosen.hook: This child-sized Pokémon can throw one hundred adults.
chosen.visualIdea: Show Machop beside a height marker, then replace one adult with a crowd of 100 silhouettes.
chosen.note: A highly specific Machop contradiction: child-sized appearance versus the canon claim that it can hurl 100 adults. The scale comparison is immediately visual and directly supported by height data and multiple Pokédex entries.

candidates.premise: Machop’s muscles never get sore or cramp, no matter how much it trains.
candidates.hook: Machop has the ultimate training advantage: its muscles never hurt.
candidates.visualIdea: Loop Machop through increasingly intense workouts while a soreness meter stays at zero.
candidates.note: A genuinely unusual biological advantage, supported across multiple entries. The soreness meter is visual, though the idea is slightly less instantly dramatic than the 100-adult claim.

candidates.premise: Machop builds strength by repeatedly carrying a Graveler like a barbell.
candidates.hook: Machop’s everyday gym equipment is another Pokémon.
candidates.visualIdea: Animate Machop lifting a Graveler across mountain reps, ending with its 100-person strength feat.
candidates.note: Very Machop-specific and easy to animate, with repeated Pokédex support. It is surprising, though familiar fans may already know the Graveler-training image.

candidates.premise: Machop reaches Machoke at level 28, but Machamp requires a trade after that.
candidates.hook: Machop’s final evolution needs something training alone can’t provide.
candidates.visualIdea: A level counter stops at 28 for Machoke, then a trade window unlocks Machamp.
candidates.note: A clear, highly visual evolution mechanic, but it is more about the game’s progression system than Machop’s identity. The cited methods are from trusted secondary data rather than the supplied Pokédex entries.

candidates.premise: After training with friends builds its confidence and muscle, Machop challenges Makuhita.
candidates.hook: Machop’s training arc ends with a very specific rival challenge.
candidates.visualIdea: Show Machop training beside friends, gaining confidence, then reveal Makuhita as the final opponent.
candidates.note: The Makuhita matchup is an excellent obscure detail and very concrete, but it relies on a single entry and does not establish that this is literally the endpoint of Machop’s training arc.

candidates.premise: Machop trains in every style of martial arts, even traveling the world to master them.
candidates.hook: Machop isn’t mastering one fighting style—it wants them all.
candidates.visualIdea: A map fills with martial-arts icons as Machop moves through each training style.
candidates.note: The training ambition is supported, but “every style” is broad and the individual martial arts are not named. The map concept risks becoming a generic montage.

rounds.request: No stronger angle is needed; this premise has the best combination of Machop-specific absurdity, reliable support, and instantly readable visuals.
